text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BRAZIL'S CENTRAL BANK CUTS IOF TAX TO ATTRACT FOREIGN CAPITAL

Brazil's Central Bank has reduced the rate of Financial Operations Tax (IOF) banks have to pay on loans secured overseas and allowed foreign investors to buy debentures convertible into shares through Annex Four rules for non-Brazilian investments.
Central Bank director Gustavo Franco said both measures are expected to increase capital inflows, contributing to offset the country's trade and current account imbalance.
-- BRAZIL QUESTIONED BY WTO
Brazil's foreign exchange policy was questioned by the World Trade Organization during its review of the country's economic and trade policy.
-- PETROBRAS ANNOUNCES OIL WELL DISCOVERY IN CAMPOS
Brazil's state oil firm Petrobras said yesterday it has struck two new oil wells in the Campos Basin, off the Rio de Janeiro coast.
The wells could add 400 million to 600 million barrels to the firm's total reserves.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- TAM'S AIRPLANE CRASHES IN SAO PAULO AND KILLS AT LEAST 97
A Fokker-100 aircraft from Brazil's TAM airline crashed in Sao Paulo two minutes after take-off at Congonhas regional airport, killing at least 97 people.
-- MAJORITY OF FLIGHT PASSENGERS WERE EXECUTIVES

The list of dead passengers from the TAM's Flight 402 include executives of banks Unibanco, Itau, Real, Boston, Santos, Citibank and Chase Manhattan Bank. The list also included executives of Coca-Cola, Esso, Hoechst, Parmalat, Siemens, Voith, Vila Romana, Teletrim, Multicanal and Generali do Brasil.
O GLOBO
-- THE DEATH IN 30 SECONDS

The Fokker-100's flight from TAM's airline bound for Rio de Janeiro lasted only 30 seconds after take-off at Congonhas regional airport. Ninety passengers, six crew members and at least two residents were killed after the plane crashed in Sao Paulo's southwest area of Jabaquara.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo newsroom, 55-11-2324411
